translationRepairs: Wang Zhixing, style name Kuangjian, was from Wen in Huazhou.
Wang Zhixing, style name Kuangjian, was from Wen in Huaizhou.
Chinese 懷州溫人 names the native place as Wen in Huaizhou; Huazhou would be 華州, so the proposed Huaizhou correction matches the source.
He was called Yan Zai at first, but later dropped the surname "Yan" and went by Zai alone.
He was called Yan Zai at first, but later dropped the generational name "Yan" and went by Zai alone.
晏宰，後去「晏」，獨名宰 drops the name element 晏 from 晏宰; calling 晏 a surname invents a false family name, while “generational name” correctly identifies the dropped given-name element.
When Zhixing returned, Qun sent staff members to welcome him and ordered the soldiers to enter in armor season by season.
When Zhixing returned, Qun sent staff members to welcome him and ordered the soldiers to enter in armor.

令士季甲而入 means the soldiers were ordered to enter armored; reading 季 as “season by season” invents a temporal sense absent from the reception scene, and dropping that phrase restores the armor sense already in the idiomatic line.
